name: Herodicus of Babylon
bio: Herodicus of Babylon was a Greek grammarian of the second century BC, a follower of Crates of Mallos and an opponent of the school of Aristarchus. The one epigram preserved under his name is a satirical attack on the Aristarchans.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the fifth volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Loeb, 1918): Book XVI: 19a.

poems.title: Book XVI, 19a
poems.author: Herodicus of Babylon
poems.text: Away with you from Greece, ye scholars of Aristarchus; take flight over the broad back of the sea, more fearful than the brown antelope, ye who buzz in corners and talk of monosyllables, whose business is “sphin” and “sphoin” and “min” and “nin.” Let these things be yours, ye fretful men, but may Hellas and divine Babylon ever remain for Herodicus.
